gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Contemporary and geometric, Redux spreads its wide letters out and swings into every curve with a visible run-up. And Noto Sans Gujarati keeps pace with large open counters, which makes it the easiest thing on the page to trust.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-go: Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi reads chunky and friendly, its lowercase as tall as a crayon mark and its terminals cut back to leave real gaps. Redux, with only a light touch of stroke modulation, sits above it as a wide-spaced display voice, so the two share a modern streak.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Redux stretches its letters wide and enters each curve with a generous lead-in, its strokes shifting a small but steady amount in thickness. Noto Sans Gurmukhi sits beside it, tidy, with outward-pointing terminals.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Noto Sans Hanunoo reads plainly, its lowercase filling most of the height. Redux feels sturdier and more deliberate beside it, because even its hairlines hold firm against the stems, while the open terminals of the sans-serif keep things easy going.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Redux has a wide-set, geometric stance, with arches that thin slightly as they leave the stem. And Noto Sans Hebrew carries a long passage with a dominant midsection and wide gaps between curve ends and stems, so the text feels generous.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-hk: Noto Sans HK sets large lowercase forms with tight ascender clearance and brush ends that lift away before each curve closes. And Redux, with its flat-brush, half-turned contrast, gives a longer passage a wide-spaced, geometric lead-in that the sans-serif then carries steadily.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-imperial-a: Redux is wide, geometric and soft in every curve. It excels at making large lettering feel contemporary, while Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic does its best work in the text, where its open c and short step up to capitals feel approachable.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-inscriptio: Redux lays out wide-spaced geometric letters with the tempered contrast of a lightly flexed spring wire. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian answers underneath with big open eyes and a deep middle band, a sans-serif that gives the display lettering room to breathe.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-jp: Noto Sans JP stands out for its very tall x-height and curves that sweep open instead of curling shut. And Redux, whose thin strokes run just slightly lighter than its thick ones, gives that text a wide-spaced, contemporary front.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Noto Sans Kaithi reads large and direct, with an open channel in the e and lowercase forms that fill the line like capitals. Redux earns its keep big and short.
